name: Multi Commodity Exchange of India Ltd
title: Multi Commodity Exchange of India Ltd - 534091 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Exchange volumes and margins at record levels: H1 PAT INR868 cr (+117% YoY), ADT INR12.6 lakh cr, but no numeric FY27 guidance and a one-off SGF reduction flatters profit.

summary.headline: MCX H1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 101% YoY to INR1,501 crore, with PAT up 117% to INR868 crore and a 75% EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Management reported half-year FY27 consolidated total income of INR1,600 crore (+99% YoY), revenue from operations of INR1,501 crore (+101% YoY), EBITDA of INR663 crore and PAT of INR868 crore (+117% YoY). Average daily turnover reached INR12.6 lakh crore, up about 20% from INR10 lakh crore in the prior quarter and nearly double a year earlier. Lower SGF contributions after a SEBI circular and a re-evaluated effective tax rate shaped the profit line, and management declined to give margin or volume guidance. The call also covered far-dated contracts, delivery-location changes effective November 2026, FPI access, and a pending data-centre migration.

segments.name: Bullion and precious metals
segments.commentary: Silver 100-gram futures launched earlier in FY27 have over INR100 crore ADT; Gold 10-gram futures are popular; silver micro-options (30 kg, 5 kg, 1 kg) are in active use. Management said expiry-day volumes in gold and silver were near INR100 lakh crore.

segments.name: Energy (electricity)
segments.commentary: Q2 ADT about INR77 crore per day versus INR57 crore per day for H1; market share about 75%; open interest about 1,500-1,600 lots, with activity in second and third months.

segments.name: Base metals
segments.commentary: Far-dated futures now run up to 12 months in aluminium, copper and zinc; management cited copper as showing strong growth and momentum, with the metals segment not expected to match precious metals.

segments.name: Crude oil and natural gas
segments.commentary: Far-dated crude contracts now extend up to 18 months. FPIs are active in cash-settled energy contracts, the only permitted segment for them currently.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance given; management declined to project quarterly or terminal EBITDA margins.
Effective tax rate expected to move closer to 25% going forward; H1 is close to 25% after a YTD catch-up booked in Q2.
SGF contributions expected to stay on hold for a couple of quarters (2-3 quarters); SEBI's August 2026 circular cut the Z-score-linked requirement from 10 to 5.
Delivery-location consolidation (lead to Chennai, zinc to Thane, mini lead to Palwal, mini zinc to Kolkata) takes effect November 2026.
Product pipeline exists but launches are being paced; announcements to follow at the appropriate time.
Management expects technology and running costs to continue as capacity grows; these are opex, not one-time.
capex_capacity: Technology capacity has been nearly doubled over recent months, with higher associated maintenance and running costs flowing into the technology expense line.
Primary matching engine and data-centre migration is under review after stakeholder consultation; management said it is not linked to FPI onboarding and no timeline was given.
Management said current capacity is well placed for near-term growth; capacity is measured by volume per day and per month.
demand_pricing: ADT rose to INR12.6 lakh crore in Q2 FY27 from INR10 lakh crore in the prior quarter.
About 250 FPIs onboarded; FPI participation is in cash-settled energy contracts, with a late single-digit share of participation.
Product license fees rose with turnover, mainly for crude pricing licensed from CME.
Bank guarantee rule change (RBI circular effective July 2026): management said prop versus retail contribution mix has not changed materially.
Management said there is no fee multiplier driving revenue; growth is attributed to volume, which is linked to volatility.
Management said market share remains above 90%, with competitive activity not yet having taken meaningful share.

qa_highlights.question: How large could SEBI's FPI access opening be, and what is the timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 250 FPIs are onboarded, volumes come from permitted cash-settled energy contracts, and wider participation depends on final SEBI circulars; no timing given.

qa_highlights.question: Why has FPI scale-up been slow despite past access and direct market access?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FPI participation is growing in the late single-digit percentages and interest is highest in India-specific contracts with price discovery and delivery linkage.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp rise in product license fees and the drop in regulatory costs?
qa_highlights.answer: License fees are turnover-linked (CME crude pricing). Regulatory costs fell because the SEBI August 2026 circular cut the SGF Z-score parameter from 10 to 5, so existing SGF contributions are sufficient for now.

qa_highlights.question: Is the effective tax rate increase a new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: A subsidiary (MCXCCL) provision and a re-evaluated annual effective tax rate were booked in Q2 as a YTD catch-up; H1 is about 25%, and the rate should trend toward 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Can premium-to-notional in options rise as longer-tenure products grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not immediate; premium-to-turnover depends on volatility, contract mix and duration, so no directional view was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the market sizing for metals versus precious metals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said metals have headroom, copper is growing strongly, but metals are not expected to reach precious-metal scale.

qa_highlights.question: Could the EBITDA margin be sustained or move toward 70-75% long term?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a terminal margin, saying investments in technology, innovation and risk will continue and that quarterly margins vary.

risks_watch: SGF buffer is expected to last only 2-3 quarters; contributions will restart afterwards, which would lift regulatory costs and compress margins.
Bank guarantee rules (RBI circular effective July 2026) may be reducing credit-funded margin; management could not quantify the impact.
Competitive intensity from rival exchange; management noted a rival's ADT growth and rising retail/algo flow but gave no market-share outlook.
Pending primary matching engine and data-centre migration: timing and cost not disclosed.
Cybersecurity exposure; management cited heightened focus after recent industry incidents.
Non-agri physical delivery policy from the SEBI circular on gold and silver is not yet formalised.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and scale, but deliberately non-committal on forward numbers: management declined to give margin, market-share or product-timing guidance, and was evasive on the bank guarantee impact and the rival exchange's performance.
key_quotes: These results demonstrate the scalability of our business model.
We don't expect that significant changes will be there when it comes to EBITDA numbers.
I don't think we really want to put a number or a projection around the EBITDA margins.
So whatever SGF contribution we have made so far is sufficient, and we don't foresee that in coming few quarters we will have to invest further.
